fit_reason: Okta sells workforce and customer identity (SSO, MFA, lifecycle management, API access management and machine-to-machine authentication through Auth0), which makes it an Identity vendor for machine and non-human identities. Every agent needs its own credentials and defined permissions before it can be given access, so identity is a precondition for agent autonomy and its demand grows as agents move from pilots to higher-stakes work. Identity is the whole business, and Okta is the leading independent cloud identity provider.

CrowdStrike runs the Falcon platform covering endpoint, cloud workload, identity protection (zero trust), threat intelligence and log management, which makes it a Security vendor with an identity and observability adjacency. Security is the most discussed agent concern after recent hacks, since a compromised or misbehaving agent holding access can do real damage, so demand for protection grows as agents are given more access. Security is the entire business, and CrowdStrike is one of the two or three largest and fastest-growing security platforms.

Palo Alto Networks sells firewalls, cloud security, SaaS security, data loss prevention and security operations, and has added AI-specific protection and privileged access through acquisitions, which makes it a Security vendor that also reaches into Identity. Security is the most discussed trust concern now, and agents that hold access to sensitive systems need guardrails and defenses against prompt injection, which is where its AI security products sit. Security is the whole business, and it is the largest pure-play cybersecurity company by revenue.

Cloudflare runs a global network selling cloud firewalls, bot mitigation, DDoS protection, zero trust access management and data protection, plus developer services such as serverless compute and an AI gateway, which makes it a Security vendor that also meters usage through a gateway and isolates code. It touches several trust parts at once: securing and identifying agent traffic, limiting and metering what it calls, and sandboxing code agents run, all of which grow with agent adoption. Security and access control are the core of the business, and Cloudflare is one of the largest edge security networks.

Zscaler sells cloud-delivered zero trust access (internet and private application access), cloud security posture management and workload segmentation, which makes it a Security vendor that enforces access policy between identities and applications. Agents need tightly scoped, policy-enforced access to systems so a compromised agent cannot move laterally, which is exactly what zero trust provides, and security is the most discussed agent concern. Security is the entire business, and Zscaler is the leading zero trust access platform.

SailPoint sells identity security and governance for human users and machine identities, governing who and what can access sensitive data and applications, which makes it an Identity and Governance vendor. Agents are non-human identities whose access has to be defined, granted and reviewed, and SailPoint's governance of machine identities fits that directly. Identity governance is the whole business, and SailPoint is the leading identity governance vendor, though smaller than the largest security platforms.

Datadog sells a SaaS observability platform covering infrastructure monitoring, application performance, log management, cloud security and incident response, which makes it an Observability vendor with a Security adjacency. Someone has to see what an agent did and what it cost, and observability vendors that trace agent and model calls are named directly in the Trust section, with cost visibility a top concern after tokenmaxxing. Observability is the core of the business, and Datadog is the leading cloud observability platform.

Microsoft sells identity (Entra), security (Defender), data governance and compliance (Purview), and runs Azure, a cloud that meters AI usage, which makes it an Identity, Security, Governance and metering-cloud vendor at once. It covers all four trust parts and its clouds and model platforms are also where controls such as spend caps get built in, so it gains as agents are adopted and is a candidate to absorb standalone controls. Trust products are a meaningful part of a much larger business, but Microsoft is one of the largest security and identity vendors in the world.

Fortinet sells FortiGate firewalls, secure networking, endpoint detection and response, web application firewalls, email security and multi-factor authentication, which makes it a Security vendor with an Identity line. Security is the most discussed agent concern, and agent traffic to sensitive systems has to pass through network and application controls. Security is the whole business, and Fortinet is one of the largest network security vendors by units shipped.

Check Point sells network, endpoint, cloud and data security under its Infinity architecture, including posture management and API security, which makes it a Security vendor. Security is the most discussed trust concern, and vendors adding agent-specific protection such as guardrails and prompt injection defenses are named in the Trust section. Security is the entire business, and Check Point is a large, long-established security vendor, though growing more slowly than the cloud-native leaders.

Dynatrace sells an observability platform covering application and microservice monitoring, infrastructure monitoring, real-time application security and digital experience, which makes it an Observability vendor. Tracing what agents did and what it cost is one of the four parts of trust, and demand grows as agents run in production. Observability is the core of the business, and Dynatrace is one of the leading enterprise application observability vendors.

SentinelOne sells the Singularity XDR platform for endpoint, cloud workload and IoT protection with AI-driven detection and response, which makes it a Security vendor. Security is the most discussed agent concern, and endpoints and workloads where agents run need protection against compromised or misbehaving code. Security is the whole business, and SentinelOne is a notable but smaller challenger to the largest endpoint vendors.

Netskope sells the Netskope One cloud security platform for data protection, secure access and visibility across SaaS, web, cloud and AI usage, which makes it a Security and data governance vendor. Agents and AI apps move sensitive data across SaaS and AI services, so controlling and seeing that flow is a direct trust need that grows with adoption. Security is the entire business, and Netskope is a recognized security service edge vendor, mid-sized next to the leaders.

fit_reason: Varonis sells data security that tracks every access to sensitive data, detects anomalous behavior, classifies data and governs access permissions, which makes it a Security and Governance vendor focused on data. Agents get access to enterprise data stores, so seeing and limiting what each identity can reach and flagging unusual access is a direct control on agents. Data security is the whole business, and Varonis is a leading specialist in data access governance.

Rubrik sells data security covering protection of enterprise, cloud and SaaS data, data threat analytics, security posture and cyber recovery, which makes it a Security vendor focused on data. A misbehaving or compromised agent can damage data, so being able to see and recover from what it did is a trust control that grows as agents get write access. Data security is the entire business, and Rubrik is a fast-growing leader in cyber recovery.

Alphabet's Google Cloud sells cybersecurity, identity and access, and AI platforms on a cloud that meters model usage, which makes it a Security vendor and a metering cloud as named in the Observability part. Clouds and model providers can build controls such as spend caps into their platforms, and Google's security business gains as agents need protection on its cloud. Trust is a meaningful but small part of a business dominated by advertising, though Google Cloud is one of the three largest clouds.

Amazon's AWS sells identity and access management, security services and AI platforms with usage metering and guardrails, which makes it an Identity, Security and metering cloud. Clouds that meter usage are named in the Trust section, and AWS is where many agents will run and have their permissions and spend set. Trust is a meaningful part of AWS but a small share of Amazon overall, and AWS is the largest cloud provider.

IBM sells security software for threat, data and identity management, AIOps and management software, and hybrid cloud, which makes it a Security, Identity and Observability vendor. These lines cover several trust parts, including identity and secrets for machine credentials, data security and operations visibility, which agents need as they get access. Trust is a meaningful part of a broad software, consulting and infrastructure business, and IBM is a large established security vendor.

Cisco sells network security, identity and access management, secure access service edge, threat detection and response, and an observability suite, which makes it a Security, Identity and Observability vendor. Agents act over networks and need controlled access and visibility, and security and observability are now a large part of Cisco's software revenue. Trust is a meaningful part of a business still led by networking equipment, and Cisco is one of the largest security vendors by revenue.

Akamai sells cloud security that shields websites, applications and APIs from attacks, along with content delivery and edge compute, which makes it a Security vendor at the edge. Agents call APIs and websites at scale, so API protection and bot management that can tell good agents from bad are direct trust needs. Security is now the main part of the business, and Akamai is a large established edge security provider.

Tenable sells exposure management, vulnerability assessment (Nessus), cloud misconfiguration detection and Active Directory security, which makes it a Security vendor. Agents add new identities and attack surface, so finding and prioritizing exposure, including identity weaknesses, is a trust need that grows with adoption. Security is the entire business, and Tenable is a leader in vulnerability management, mid-sized next to the platform leaders.

ServiceNow sells governance, risk and compliance, security operations and IT operations management on its workflow platform, which makes it a Governance vendor with a Security operations line. Governance of what agents may do, with policies and permissions, is one of the four trust parts, and agents running inside enterprise workflows need oversight from the platform where the work runs. Trust is a meaningful part of a larger workflow business, and ServiceNow is a major enterprise platform.

Elastic sells the Elastic Stack for search and analytics, with logging, application performance monitoring and host security built on it, which makes it an Observability and Security vendor. Seeing what agents did through logs and traces, and detecting threats in that data, are both trust parts that grow with agent adoption. Observability and security are central to the business alongside search, and Elastic is a well-known mid-sized vendor in both.

F5 sells application delivery and security, including web application firewalls, API protection, access policy management, bot and fraud defense and multi-cloud traffic control, which makes it a Security vendor in the gateway path. Gateways that sit in front of applications and APIs can secure, limit and meter agent traffic, which the Trust section names. Application security and access control are central to the business, and F5 is a large established application delivery vendor.

Qualys sells a cloud platform for vulnerability management, threat detection, endpoint security, patch management and compliance, which makes it a Security vendor. Exposure and vulnerability management protect the systems agents act on, a trust need that rises with security concerns. Security is the entire business, and Qualys is an established, highly profitable mid-sized vendor.

AvePoint sells data governance, policy enforcement, access and entitlement insight, and backup for Microsoft, Google, Salesforce and other cloud platforms, which makes it a Governance vendor focused on data. AI assistants and agents surface whatever data they can reach, so governing permissions and data before agents are deployed is a direct trust need. Governance is the core of the business, and AvePoint is a small but focused vendor.

Commvault sells a cyber resilience platform for backup, threat scanning in backup data, cyber recovery and compliance logging, which makes it a Security vendor focused on data recovery. Agents with write access can damage data, so recovering cleanly from what they did is a trust control, though less directly tied to agents than identity or guardrails. Security is a meaningful framing of a business rooted in data protection, and Commvault is a large established vendor.

Fastly runs an edge cloud with DDoS protection, web application firewall, API and account takeover protection, bot mitigation and authentication, alongside content delivery, which makes it a Security vendor at the edge. Bot management and API protection help separate trusted agents from abusive ones at scale. Security is a meaningful part of a business still led by delivery, and Fastly is a small player next to Cloudflare and Akamai.

PagerDuty sells an operations management platform that ingests signals from software systems and uses machine learning for incident detection and response, which makes it an Observability-adjacent vendor. Seeing and responding to what automated systems, including agents, do in production is part of observability. Operations visibility is the core of the business, but PagerDuty is a small player.

Radware sells DDoS protection, web application firewalls, Kubernetes WAF and application delivery controllers, which makes it a Security vendor. Agents call applications at scale, so application and bot protection are trust needs. Security is the main part of the business, but Radware is a small vendor.

Gen Digital sells consumer cyber safety, including Norton 360, identity theft protection (LifeLock), VPN and privacy tools, which makes it a Security and Identity vendor for consumers. Consumer AI agents acting on a person's behalf create new fraud and account risks, though the Trust section is centered on enterprise controls for agents. Security is the whole business, and Gen is the largest consumer security vendor.

Mastercard runs a payments network with cyber and intelligence solutions, digital identity and tokenized secure transactions, which makes it a Governance and Identity vendor for agent spending. Agents that buy things need identity, spend limits and fraud controls at the payment layer, and cost control is one of the top trust concerns. Trust products are a meaningful part of a network business, and Mastercard is one of the two global card networks.

Workiva sells a cloud platform for compliance and regulatory reporting with granular permissions, audit trails and GRC integration, which makes it a Governance vendor. Audit trails and governed workflows matter as agents start touching regulated reporting, but its link to agent controls is indirect. Governance and compliance are central to the business, and Workiva is a mid-sized leader in its niche.

JFrog sells a software supply chain platform with Artifactory, CI/CD and Xray security scanning of packages, which makes it a Security and Governance vendor for the code and models agents run. Controlling which code, packages and models are allowed into production is a governance and security need that agents raise. Security is a meaningful and growing part of a business built on artifact management, and JFrog is a mid-sized vendor.

A10 Networks sells application delivery controllers plus DDoS protection, SSL inspection and convergent firewalls, which makes it a Security vendor in the traffic path. Securing and inspecting application traffic, including agent traffic, is a trust need. Security is a meaningful part of a business also built on load balancing and carrier networking, and A10 is a small player.

NetScout sells service assurance and network monitoring, plus Arbor DDoS defense and threat detection, which makes it an Observability and Security vendor. Visibility into network traffic and defense against attacks support trust in systems agents use. These lines are the business, but the link to agent controls is indirect and NetScout is a small, slow-growing vendor.

OpenText sells information management software plus security and cyber resilience products (Carbonite, Webroot, forensic tools), which makes it partly a Security vendor. Securing and governing enterprise content matters as agents read it, but security is one line among many. Security is a meaningful part of a larger information management business, and OpenText is a large but slow-growing vendor.

BlackBerry sells cybersecurity (endpoint protection, detection and response, zero trust access, unified endpoint management) alongside its QNX embedded software and secure communications, which makes it partly a Security vendor. Securing devices and endpoints supports trust, but its offerings are not focused on agents. Security is a meaningful part of the business next to IoT, and BlackBerry is a small player in security.

Bill.com sells cloud accounts payable, receivable and spend management with card spend controls for small and mid-sized businesses, which makes it a borderline Governance vendor for spend. Spend limits are named in the Trust section as a governance control, and the same card controls could apply to agent purchases. Spend management is a meaningful part of the business, but Bill is a small player in agent controls and the fit is borderline.

Navan sells corporate travel and expense management with booking, payments and policy enforcement, which makes it a borderline Governance vendor for spend. Enforcing spend policy is a named governance control, and agent-booked travel would need the same limits. Policy enforcement is central to its product, but the agent link is speculative and the fit is borderline.

Corpay sells corporate payments including virtual cards, purchasing and travel cards and fleet cards with spend controls, which makes it a borderline Governance vendor for spend. Virtual cards with per-transaction limits are one way to cap what agents spend, a named trust concern. Spend control is part of the product, but the business is payments and the fit is borderline.

WEX sells fleet payments, virtual cards for travel and corporate payments, and spend management tools, which makes it a borderline Governance vendor for spend. Virtual cards with controls could cap agent spending, which the Trust section names. Spend control is part of the product but the business is payments, and the fit is borderline.

Marqeta runs a modern card issuing platform with configurable cards and issuer processing, which makes it a borderline Governance vendor for spend. Programmable cards with just-in-time funding and spend rules are a natural way to cap what agents spend. Spend controls are central to its product, but it is a small player and the fit is borderline.

TransUnion sells credit reporting plus identity verification, authentication, and fraud and identity management solutions, which makes it a borderline Identity vendor focused on people. Verifying the person behind an agent and preventing fraud become more important as agents transact, but the Trust section's identity is about agent credentials. Identity and fraud is a meaningful part of the business, and TransUnion is a major credit bureau.

Equifax sells credit data plus identity verification, fraud detection and identity management, which makes it a borderline Identity vendor focused on people. Identity verification and fraud prevention matter as agents act for people, though the Trust section centers on agent credentials. Identity and fraud is a meaningful part of the business, and Equifax is a major credit bureau.

Red Violet sells identity intelligence for verification, due diligence and fraud prevention, which makes it a borderline Identity vendor focused on people. Verifying identities behind transactions gains as agents act for people, but the link to agent credentials is indirect. Identity intelligence is the whole business, but Red Violet is a very small player.

Clear Secure runs a biometric identity verification platform for members, best known for airport security lanes, which makes it a borderline Identity vendor focused on people. Verified human identity could anchor which person an agent acts for, but its business today is consumer travel. Identity verification is central to the business, but its fit with agent identity is borderline.

Progress Software sells application development tools plus secure file transfer (MOVEit), infrastructure automation (Chef) and network monitoring, which makes it marginally an Observability and Security vendor. These products give some visibility and control over systems agents use, but they are not agent controls. Trust is a small part of a development tools business, and Progress is a small player.

Alibaba's cloud sells computing, security and database services on a cloud that meters usage, which makes it a metering cloud with a Security line. Clouds that meter usage and offer security are named in the Trust section, mainly for agents running in China. Trust is a small part of a commerce-led business, and Alibaba Cloud is the largest cloud in China.
